correctness.rationale: Every three-factor permutation product differs by a central commutator offset; an invertible F_p-linear transformation expresses the six offsets as three signed pairs ±x,±y,±z for odd p. GL3 congruence is transitive on nonzero alternating 3×3 Gram data, and counting orthogonal triples gives Z=p^(2d)+(p^d−1)p^(2d−3). All nonzero Gram triples have common mass α=(1−p^(−d))/p³; signed pair occupancy yields the six probabilities. Independent exact enumeration for p=3,5,7 reproduced N_k=(1, 4(p−1),9(p−1),6(p−1)(p−3),3(p−1)(p−3),(p−1)(p−3)(p−5)) with the zero tuple handled separately. Proof valid for both odd extraspecial types, m≥1; no claim for p=2.
